Market today: The mood is mixed. Fed minutes show growing support for rate hikes, which is a headwind for your tech/chip names. However, Treasury action on debt repurchases pulled yields back, offering some relief. The real driver is the ongoing tug-of-war between inflation fears and potential yield stabilization.

Your holdings: SOXL (-52.03%) and SPAL (-40.68%) are leveraged, decaying ETFs with deep losses and ineffective default stops. Margin amplifies these drops. SMH (-11.5%) and QQQI (-3.53%) are also flagged for trimming and are close to their stops.

Watch: Keep a close eye on bond yields and any further Fed commentary. Also, monitor the stops on SMH and QQQI as they are approaching critical levels.

Bottom line: Prioritize risk management on your leveraged and underperforming positions, especially with the Fed's hawkish tone.
plays: Re-evaluate stops for SOXL and SPAL; their current default stops are not protective given deep losses and leveraged decay.
Watch SMH (stop 540) and QQQI (stop 52) closely; be ready to trim if stops are hit.
Consider a new buy on MRVL (entry 233.26-232.93, stop 228.44) given the positive Google customer news and scanner setup.
